title: A flow's morning run still happens when the Mac reaches the slot late
description: On the Owner's Mac every scheduled 06:00 fire of the saturation flow from 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-18 was recorded as missed: the timer woke 1.0 to 3.3 seconds after the slot, the scheduler's grace is one second, and flows/neighborhood-activation/stream.json says catch_up skip. No scheduled cycle ever ran; only runs started by hand drafted anything, so Today emptied as its drafts aged out. The shipped stream says catch_up run_once, so the scheduler fires the newest late slot once (the Supervisor's gates still decide the fire). A stream registered before this change keeps its stored definition, so when fwd starts, before the scheduler is armed, each registered flow stream whose late-slot rule differs from its shipped stream.json is rewritten the way a moved cron is: a new version, a new definition hash and one stream.updated event. A copy follows its base flow. The scheduler's grace and the other flows' streams are unchanged.
acceptance: flows/neighborhood-activation/stream.json has trigger.catch_up run_once, and turning the flow on registers a stream that carries it
A scheduler that reaches the flow's cron slot 90 seconds late records that slot once as fired and records no missed row for it
A stream registered earlier with catch_up skip says run_once after fwd starts, with a higher version and exactly one stream.updated event; a second start changes nothing
The Supervisor's gates still hold a late fire the way they hold one on time
